macvideoplayer includes FFmpeg 9.0.2, Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers.
https://ffmpeg.org/

This software uses FFmpeg code licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public
License version 2.1 or later (LGPL). The full license is in COPYING.LGPLv2.1.
The unmodified corresponding source is supplied alongside this notice as
ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz. Component licensing details are in LICENSE.md and the
source archive. FFmpeg is provided without warranty; see the license.

The libraries are dynamically linked and embedded in Contents/Frameworks:
libavformat, libavcodec, libavfilter, libavutil, libswscale, libswresample.
No FFmpeg command-line programs are included or executed.

Source: https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz
SHA-256: 8c3850283eb25fa026482078a04051e0be17347b09ef81a0849bec15a96e002e

Build: Apple clang, macOS SDK, deployment target macOS 12.4, arm64 and x86_64.
No GPL, nonfree or optional third-party dependencies were enabled. Automatic
external-library discovery was disabled. Apple system frameworks, zlib,
bzip2 and iconv are the only non-FFmpeg dependencies. The exact build commands
are in build-ffmpeg.sh; run it with a destination directory to rebuild the
libraries from the supplied source. Xcode signs the dylibs when embedding them.

You may modify and replace these LGPL libraries for your own use and reverse
engineer macvideoplayer as needed to debug those modifications, as permitted by the LGPL.
For a local development copy, replace the corresponding dylibs under
Contents/Frameworks and re-sign the app and libraries with your own development
identity (or an ad-hoc signature for local use). The original distributor's
signature cannot remain valid after a modification. No FFmpeg source changes
were made by macvideoplayer.
